extracted.intended_audience: aspiring and practicing conjurers/prestidigitators, automata makers, and readers interested in historical practice and presentation of magic and mechanical wonders
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative principles for designing and presenting prestidigitation performances and automata exhibitions, drawn from historical practice and contemporaneous critical reports. Covers act composition, audience management, mechanical ingenuity, demonstration and publicity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tailor acts to audience: mystifications for gentlemen, compliments for ladies, puns for all
rubrics_metrics.description: «la base fondamentale des séances de Comte était les mystifications aux Messieurs (les souverains exceptés), les compliments aux Dames et les calembours à tout le monde.»
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use different kinds of effects to suit different audience segments: mystifications to intrigue/astound certain viewers, polite compliments to flatter ladies, and lighter wordplay for general amusement. The choice of such elements contributed to Comte's usual success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid calembours (puns) in public prestidigitation
rubrics_metrics.description: «Le calembour... il provoque un rire qui nuit nécessairement à l'intérêt de ses expériences.»
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer astonishment over laughter: «Mieux vaut l'étonnement cent fois que le fou rire.» Puns often cause uproarious laughter which leaves no durable memory of the effect and thus undermines the interest and mystery of a magic demonstration; they may be acceptable in informal workshops but not in formal performances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refrain from perfumed/symbolic compliments and staging spectators
rubrics_metrics.description: «Le langage symbolique, complimenteur et parfumé, est aussi complètement tombé en désuétude... les dames qui assistent à une séance de prestidigitation, y viennent pour se récréer l'esprit et non pour être elles‑mêmes mises en scène.»
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid putting audience members (especially ladies) into the spotlight with over-polished compliments or staged flattery; spectators typically prefer to remain simple observers rather than be made the object of direct, pointed gallantry during a magic show.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mystification is an acceptable technique but should be used with judgement
rubrics_metrics.description: Discussion of Comte's use of mystification and the author's ambivalence: some defend mystification as an effective means while others may object.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mystification (deliberate deception/cover stories) can be a powerful tool to produce astonishment or practical advantage (e.g., escape, concealment), but its use is ethically and artistically debatable; different practitioners succeed with different principles. Balance audience expectation and taste when choosing to mystify.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid the boring genre: novelty and interest are paramount
rubrics_metrics.description: «Tous les genres sont bons, hors le genre ennuyeux.»
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whatever stylistic choices are made, the overriding criterion is to avoid boredom — originality, variety and maintaining audience interest trump strict adherence to any single style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanical ingenuity and inventiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: From the Academy's report on Vaucanson: the machine was judged «extrêmement ingénieuse» and employed «des moyens simples et nouveaux» to achieve its effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate automata by the cleverness and novelty of their mechanisms: solutions that are both ingenious and based on simple, effective means are especially valued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accurate imitation of human/animal functions in automata
rubrics_metrics.description: The Academy praised Vaucanson for imitating by art «tout ce que l'homme est obligé de faire» (movements of fingers, varying wind into a flute, valves acting as tongue, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A high-quality automaton convincingly reproduces the target biological motions and behaviors (finger work, breath modulation, articulation) in a way that is faithful enough to impress and convince observers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and precision in technical description
rubrics_metrics.description: The Academy observed that Vaucanson's Mémoire «avait toute la clarté et la précision dont cette matière est susceptible; ce qui prouve l'intelligence de l'auteur et ses grandes connaissances dans les différentes parties de la mécanique.»
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When documenting or presenting mechanical inventions, clear, precise written descriptions (and demonstrations) are essential evidence of understanding and competence and aid critical recognition by peers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scrutinize grand claims (transparency about simulated functions)
rubrics_metrics.description: The author describes how Vaucanson's claimed digestion in the canard was in fact a prepared mystification: the 'digestion' was mechanically simulated with prepared colored mixture and pump.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims that an automaton reproduces complex organic processes should be examined critically; simulated effects (artifice) do not necessarily diminish the inventor's skill but should be understood as constructed phenomena rather than literal biological replication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public demonstration, challenge posters and marketing increase fame and revenue
rubrics_metrics.description: Vaucanson presented at fairs (foire de Saint‑Germain) and Paris with great receipts; Kempelen and company used posters (e.g., challenge to strong players) and touring exhibitions to attract crowds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Successful presentation strategy includes public exhibitions, advertised challenges, and touring performances; good publicity and spectacle can be as important as mechanical merit for widespread recognition and financial success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional naming/branding should reflect merit
rubrics_metrics.description: Jules de Rovère coined the title 'prestidigitateur' to elevate his status and the author states: «il vaut mieux honorer sa profession que d'être honoré par elle.»
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A professional title or brand is useful, but genuine reputation must be built through merit and craft; select nomenclature that supports the desired professional image while relying on demonstrated skill.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of convincing but possibly simulated interior mechanisms for misdirection
rubrics_metrics.description: Description of Kempelen's chess automaton: visible gears and mechanisms inside the cabinet were a simulacrum that folded away to leave space for a hidden human player.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When demonstrating an automaton, apparent transparency (showing interior workings) can itself be engineered as mise-en-scène to misdirect observers; designing convincing but non‑functional visible mechanisms can protect secrets and heighten the impression of mechanical autonomy.
